extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (social scientists) preparing LOIs and full proposals for Russell Sage Foundation Core Research Grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing a Letter of Inquiry (LOI) and invited full proposals for Russell Sage Foundation Core Research Grants, focused on multidisciplinary social-science research using administrative or large-scale survey data. Emphasizes project readiness and alignment with RSF program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Application not perceived to be well-aligned with the Foundation's funding priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure their topic and research questions map to RSF program areas (Behavioral Economics; Decision Making and Human Behavior in Context; Future of Work; Race, Ethnicity, and Immigration; Social, Political, and Economic Inequality; Special Initiatives). Lack of alignment is a common reason for decline at initial screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient detail (research design, data, methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lacks sufficient detail on the research design, data, and methods to allow reviewers to assess the viability of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOIs should include enough methodological detail for assessment; reviewers expect clear description of data sources, analytic approach, identification strategies, and other design features. Insufficient methodological detail leads to initial decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor framing or writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is poorly framed or written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, well-framed prose is important; poor framing/writing is a frequent reason for early rejection. Present the hypothesis, contribution, and design succinctly and coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit — one of the evaluation standards used by RSF when awarding grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are evaluated (and grants awarded) based on Merit along with Feasibility and Potential impact; demonstrate intellectual importance and contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility — one of the evaluation standards used by RSF when awarding grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the project is achievable given the timeline, team expertise, data access, and proposed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential impact — one of the evaluation standards used by RSF when awarding grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe expected contributions to knowledge, policy relevance, and how findings will affect understanding or interventions related to inequality and social problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis (Required LOI element)
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs should present the hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use most LOI space to state clear hypotheses that the proposed analyses will test; hypotheses should connect to theory and the study's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of the data (Required LOI element)
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs should describe the appropriateness of the data for the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the selected data sources are suitable for answering the research question, including coverage, measures, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and power calculations (Required LOI element)
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs should include sample size and power calculations for quantitative studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide power calculations or justification that sample size is sufficient to detect meaningful effects; reviewers assess statistical power as part of viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary or pilot findings (Required LOI element)
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs should report preliminary or pilot findings if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any pilot analyses or initial results (when data are available) to demonstrate feasibility and promise; absence of preliminary work can weaken an LOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design (Required LOI element)
rubrics_metrics.description: LOIs should describe the research design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify empirical strategy, identification approach, variables, timelines, and steps to carry out the study; detailed design helps reviewers judge viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — fully-developed research design
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF rarely considers projects for which the investigators have NOT already fully-developed the research design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for proposals where the research design is already completed and clearly articulated before applying; undeveloped designs reduce funding likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — sample framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should have already fully-developed the sample framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should define sample selection rules, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and sampling plans in advance of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — access to data
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should have already secured access to data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RSF prefers projects where data access is in place; lack of data access is a common barrier. For public data, preliminary analyses are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — survey instruments pre-tested
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should have developed and pre-tested survey instruments (when applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For studies involving original data collection, RSF expects finalized and pre-tested instruments prior to full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — preliminary data analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should have some preliminary data analyses (if data publicly available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary analyses strengthen an application by demonstrating feasibility and familiarity with the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project readiness — preliminary qualitative interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should have conducted some preliminary interviews for qualitative studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial qualitative work signals readiness and helps refine research questions and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of newly available data (Research priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses that make use of newly available data are of particular interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate novel empirical leverage by applying fresh administrative or survey data recently released or newly access-enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel uses of existing data (Research priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate novel uses of existing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative measurement, linkage, or analytic approaches applied to existing datasets are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering emerging or long-standing questions (Research priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that answer emerging or long-standing questions of interest in foundation program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the study to address important unanswered questions relevant to RSF's focus on inequality and social problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-disciplinary review process
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF employs rigorous multi-disciplinary review at every stage; LOIs and proposals are reviewed by program staff, external reviewers from multiple disciplines, and members of Advisory Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect evaluation by diverse experts; present methods, theory, and contributions clearly for both specialists and reviewers from other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral Economics (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral Economics — decisions in real-world settings and implications of behavioral findings for policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame research to illuminate behavior in context and to draw policy-relevant implications from behavioral evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Making and Human Behavior in Context (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision Making and Human Behavior in Context — social/cultural context shaping decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize contextual factors and mechanisms through which social and cultural influences shape decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future of Work (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Future of Work — technology, automation, and labor market change; workforce inequality and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should engage with labor-market transformations, inequality dynamics, and policy responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race, Ethnicity, and Immigration (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Race, Ethnicity, and Immigration — inequality across racial/ethnic groups; immigration policy and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address disparities, mechanisms, and policy impacts related to race, ethnicity, and immigration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social, Political, and Economic Inequality (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social, Political, and Economic Inequality — trends, causes and consequences, policy interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should connect to inequality dynamics and potential interventions or policy levers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Initiatives (Program area priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Initiatives (rotating) — e.g., pandemic effects, AI and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RSF supports time-sensitive or rotating priority topics; proposals addressing current special initiatives may be prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for fully-developed projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong preference for fully-developed research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RSF favors applications where major design decisions, data access, and preliminary work are complete prior to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-disciplinary social science focus
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF has a multi-disciplinary social science focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that bridge disciplines or demonstrate relevance across social science fields align well with RSF's review approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy use of administrative data and large-scale surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF favors heavy use of administrative data and large-scale surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects leveraging high-quality administrative sources or large-scale survey datasets are particularly suited to RSF priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on inequality and social problems
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF focuses on inequality and social problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame contributions in terms of implications for inequality, policy, and social problem mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of preliminary work before applying
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF encourages preliminary work before applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct pilot analyses, secure data access, pre-test instruments, and gather initial qualitative evidence to strengthen LOIs and full proposals.
